_purpose: Columns the approved TAD §3.1 names that are NOT YET in solution source, each ACCEPTED for now with an owner, a reason, the action that clears it, and a dated expiry. Read by scripts/verify-tad-coverage.py (C-TECH-066) and by nothing else.
_why: verify-tad-coverage.py is HARD: a column the approved architecture names and source does not hold is a schema defect that every other gate in this repository is structurally blind to, because an absent column is absent from both sides of every source-against-source comparison (IMP-0159). But phased delivery means some of those columns are legitimately not built yet, and a gate that is switched off because reality violates it is the gate-cannot-fail class arriving by the front door (contract/known-exceptions.json, _why). So absences are not waived silently: they are enumerated here, owned, dated, and re-reported on every run. This file deliberately mirrors known-exceptions.json's shape and its rule.
_not_a_waiver: A deferral suppresses the FAIL for the columns it names, never the report. Every run prints the deferred count in its summary line, and an expired deferral FAILS.
_required_fields: id, table, columns, reason, owner, clears_when, expires — all seven, on every entry. A deferral missing any of them FAILS the gate, and so does one whose `expires` is in the past or is not an ISO YYYY-MM-DD date. That is the point: an unowned or undated deferral is indistinguishable from a column nobody has noticed is missing, which is the exact state this gate was built to end.
_columns_field: Either the string "*", meaning every column TAD §3.1 names on that table (used when the TABLE itself does not exist in source yet), or an explicit array of column logical names. Prefer the array: "*" defers a whole table's schema, so it hides a column added to §3.1 afterwards.
_stale_entries_fail: A deferral that matches no absent §3.1 column FAILS as a dead promise — either the columns shipped or the TAD changed. Delete the entry when it is satisfied; a deferral file that accumulates satisfied entries becomes a blanket nobody reads.

deferrals.reason: TAD §3.1 states the column conditionally — 'Only if actually captured — SDD OQ-027 open'. SDD OQ-027 (plan §Open Questions) asks whether ethnic group is captured at all and assigns the answer to Emily / the DPO before DPIA sign-off. Building the column now would create an Article 9 surface the DPIA has not accepted, and no accepted WBS task names ethnicity capture — so the column is a change-order or WBS-resolution decision (C-COM-002) before any schema work, not an omission to fix in Entity.xml. Deferred here rather than left bare because a HARD gate failing on a question nobody has been asked teaches people to route around the gate.
deferrals.clears_when: OQ-027 is answered. If ethnicity IS captured: the work resolves to an accepted WBS task or a change order, the column is built with its column-security binding, and this entry is deleted. If it is NOT captured: TAD §3.1's conditional row is amended to drop it, and this entry is deleted. Either way the entry goes away — it is not renewed by default.
deferrals.expiry_rationale: SHORT ON PURPOSE, and not inherited from any phase date. This is a question, not a build: four weeks is enough to ask it and long enough that the gate does not cry wolf. A Phase 3 date (2026-11-27) would hide an unasked question for three months, which is the state IMP-0159 already found once.

deferrals.reason: TAD §3.1 groups it with `rev_wellbeinganswer1..n` and `rev_incomeband` as the score inputs (FR-013, FR-016). Source holds rev_wellbeinganswer1..rev_wellbeinganswer10 and rev_incomeband; nothing named rev_financialanswers exists, and the Phase 1 scoring engine shipped without reading it. Whether FR-013 needs a separate column at all, or is already satisfied by those eleven, is an architecture decision — and either answer needs a resolved WBS task before schema work, because automation #2's tasks are claimed complete (C-COM-002). Guessing a shape for a scoring input is exactly the class of invention this repository refuses (IMP-0011).
deferrals.clears_when: architect-agent rules on FR-013's inputs. If the eleven existing columns satisfy it: TAD §3.1 drops the name and this entry is deleted. If a real column is needed: it resolves to an accepted task or a change order, is built, and this entry is deleted.
deferrals.expiry_rationale: Short by design — a design ruling on an already-delivered automation, not new build work. It must resurface in four weeks rather than ride a phase date, because the scoring engine is live and every day it runs is a day it may be scoring on the wrong input set.

deferrals.reason: The five columns FR-023/FR-024/FR-025 need: check a new application against QuickBooks grant history at create time and record the prior grant's reference, date and amount on the APPLICATION. No accepted WBS task writes them. Task 4.3/4.4 (intake, claimed Done) do no QuickBooks lookup, and task 7.2 flags a possible double-pay on the PAYMENT row, not the application — so the application-side half of FR-023–025 is unquoted work today. That makes it a change-order or WBS-resolution decision for commercial-agent (C-COM-002) before any schema work, which is why these are deferred rather than built: building them would be delivery against no contract line.
deferrals.clears_when: commercial-agent resolves FR-023–025's application-side columns to an accepted WBS task or a change order. They are then built under it and this entry is deleted. If the decision is that the duplicate flag lives on Payment only, TAD §3.1's rev_application row is amended instead and this entry is deleted.
deferrals.expiry_rationale: Short by design — this is a commercial decision that needs no build to make, and it is the one deferral here with hours attached. Riding a phase date would let unquoted work sit undecided until the phase that cannot pay for it.

deferrals.reason: Both belong to automation #5 (narrative scrubbing): WBS 5.3 builds the scrubbing flow and 5.4 builds confidence flagging. FR-029's threshold comparison and the human-in-the-loop withholding gate have no writer until 5.4 lands, and neither task has started. contract/known-exceptions.json EX-003 already records the reviewer's decision to defer automation #5 (5.1–5.7) while the trustee portal is built ahead of it, with the compensating control named there (trustee visibility is bound to rev_narrativeredacted and the raw narrative never leaves REV_TrusteeRestricted). This entry mirrors that accepted decision for the schema gate; the columns are contracted, not unquoted, so no change order is needed — only the tasks running.
deferrals.clears_when: WBS 5.3/5.4 land, these two columns are built with the flow that writes them, and this entry is deleted. rev_redactionreleased already exists, so the pair completes FR-029's control rather than starting it.
deferrals.expiry_rationale: Inherited from EX-003 and Phase 3's contractual due date, deliberately NOT shortened: the same absence is already owned and dated there, and two mechanisms holding different deadlines for one absence is how a deferral quietly outlives its exception. Same inheritance rule as TD-001–004.

_no_schema_work_without_a_task: None of TD-005 to TD-008 authorises building a column. Each names the decision that must land first — an answer to SDD OQ-027, an architecture ruling on FR-013, a commercial resolution of FR-023–025, or the tasks 5.3/5.4 actually running. Adding the attribute to Entity.xml before that is delivery against no contract line (C-COM-002), which is the failure the deferral exists to prevent, not the fix it is asking for.
